clue.text: Beginning to address many burning issues, to an extent

indicators.note: the beginning of each of the next five words is taken, their initial letters running together

explanation.surface: Tackling a heap of hot topics only goes so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' applies to every word from 'address' to 'to', so the initials spell the answer; 'an extent' is left as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the scope or range of something, so it is a synonym for an extent.

clue.text: Accumulated bill on island finally settled

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
Crete is the Greek island

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An account settled at last on a Mediterranean island has built up.
explanation.definitionFit: Accreted means grown by gradual addition, so it is a synonym for accumulated.

clue.text: Engaged lad interrupted by daughter who meddles

parts.note: engaged, like a phone line, means busy

indicators.note: interrupted by means the word is broken open and the letter put inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A preoccupied young man gets interrupted by his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who meddles' defines a person: the busybody is one who meddles.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody is a nosy person who interferes in other people's business, one who meddles.

clue.text: He drew people from French city to the other French clubs

parts.note: Toulouse is a city in south-west France
l'autre is French for the other
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: An artist sketched people on a trip from one French city to some nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec drew the dancers and drinkers of Paris cabarets, which suits the 'clubs' of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Toulouse-Lautrec was a French artist famous for drawings and posters of Montmartre nightlife figures.

clue.text: Union members enjoying two affiliations

parts.note: reads like trade unionists holding two memberships, but the union is marriage and the two affiliations are two spouses at once

explanation.surface: Trade unionists who belong to two organisations at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: People who marry a second spouse while still married are members of two marital unions at once.

clue.text: Born north of the border — a minor inconvenience

indicators.note: in a down clue, north of means placed above, so first

parts.note: a lip is the border or rim of something

explanation.surface: Being born in Scotland is presented as a small nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north of the border' suggests Scotland, but it only places B above LIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A blip is a temporary minor problem or hiccup, a small inconvenience.

clue.text: Refuse to enter this, being

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held and printed (scan) as 'Refuse to enter this, being' with no letter count: cut short at the column foot, and a search found the rest nowhere.

clue.text: Mediocre cars shouldn't cross it

definitions.meaning: the central line of a road, which traffic should not stray over

explanation.surface: Dull drivers stay away from the white line.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road describes moderate, unexciting views or tastes, and literally the road's centre line.

clue.text: Go away without English subje? for painting

definitions.note: the page prints a garbled 'subje?', plainly the word subject: the thing a painting depicts

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the first word surrounds the letter

parts.note: scram is a command to go away

explanation.surface: A painter is told to leave because his subject is not English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside. Munch's painting The Scream is the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Munch's famous painting The Scream takes a scream as its subject.

clue.text: Fool with straw in mouth?

definitions.meaning: a gullible person who is easily taken in
someone sipping through a straw, or a young animal suckling, draws liquid with the mouth

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin chewing on a piece of straw.
explanation.definitionFit: A sucker is a dupe, and also one who sucks, as through a drinking straw.

clue.text: Mercutio's prepared, fashioned by me

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters of the name are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatrical outfitter boasts of having made the costume for Mercutio in Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by the outfitter: the anagram of MERCUTIOS gives the answer, and the costume for Mercutio prepared by 'me' defines who is speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A costumier makes or supplies costumes, so a stage character's outfit would be fashioned by one.

clue.text: Physicist I introduced to wit from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left, so the letters run backwards
introduced to means the letter is put inside the word for wit

parts.note: a card is a witty or eccentric person, a bit of a wag

explanation.surface: A scientist claims he brought a joker in from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced to' puts I inside CARD to make CARID, and 'from the east' turns it round. Paul Dirac was the British physicist of quantum theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dirac was a Nobel-winning theoretical physicist, so his surname is an example of a physicist.

clue.text: Close bar, missing finals at the same time

indicators.note: missing finals means each of the two words loses its last letter

parts.note: the close of something is its end
to bar is to block

explanation.surface: A pub shuts its bar early, the last orders all going together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing finals' drops the last letter of both words: END loses D and BLOCK loses K. EN BLOC is French for all together.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc, borrowed from French, means all together as one unit, so happening at the same time.

clue.text: Female, Craig's other half, starts to feel emotionally secure

parts.note: Ailsa Craig is an island rock in the Firth of Clyde, so Ailsa is the other half of its name

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A woman, Craig's partner, begins to feel safe in her relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craig's other half' looks like a wife or girlfriend; it is AILSA, from Ailsa Craig, a Scottish island off the Ayrshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A fail-safe system is built to stay safe even when something goes wrong, so it is secure.

clue.text: In despair, Joe beat up menace

indicators.note: to beat up is to batter something, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Joe, in despair, gets violent and threatens someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeopardise something is to put it at risk, so to threaten or menace it.

clue.text: Do knees break to reveal what's inside us?

indicators.note: to break the words is to smash them apart and rearrange their letters

parts.note: to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: An X-ray asks whether breaking your knees shows what lies within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges DOKNEES into ENDOSKE; LET ON (reveal) completes it. The question mark marks the definition as playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans have an internal skeleton, the bony frame inside the body, as opposed to a shell outside it.

clue.text: Girl sick at heart to be in Juliet's place

indicators.note: to be in means those letters go inside the place name

parts.note: Verona is the Italian city where Shakespeare's Juliet lived

indicators.note: at heart means the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A girl, lovesick, longs to be where Juliet was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Juliet's place' is not her balcony or her role but her home city in Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Outcome of strike — servant must occupy empty box-office

indicators.note: must occupy means the word for servant fills the space in the middle
empty means the inside is cleared out, leaving the first and last letters

parts.note: a lackey is a servant or footman

explanation.surface: A walkout by staff leaves the theatre box office deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action, but it means a punch. BOX-OFFICE emptied leaves B and E around LACKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A black eye is the bruise left after a blow to the face, the result of being struck.

clue.text: I'd never forget to secure a large animal

parts.note: an elephant never forgets, as the saying goes, so this is what one might say
to seal is to secure or close tightly

explanation.surface: Someone vows to remember to lock something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'd never forget' sounds like a promise; it is the voice of the proverbial elephant that never forgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant seals are the biggest seals, males weighing several tonnes, so certainly a large animal.

clue.text: Go work in post office, collecting fines

indicators.note: in means the work goes inside the abbreviation for post office

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
collecting says the post office takes fines along after it; F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine, so two fines give FF

explanation.surface: Someone heads off to a job at the post office, picking up fines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is the definition in the sense of die: to pop off.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop off is an informal idiom for dying, as is go in the euphemistic sense.

clue.text: Almost choose fine piece of cake

indicators.note: almost means each of the two words is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: to pick is to choose
nice can mean fine or pleasant

explanation.surface: Advice on nearly settling for a decent slice of gateau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from both PICK and NICE. 'Piece of cake' is the idiom for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is idiomatically an easy task, as in 'no picnic', just like a piece of cake.

clue.text: Passing notice

parts.note: seems to mean a brief glance, but passing is dying and the notice is a published report of it

explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper item marking someone's death, with an account of their life, is a notice of their passing.

clue.text: Ultimately, eighth unfinished symphony is larger than life

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the final letter of the next word is used
unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony

explanation.surface: Musical talk about a grand, incomplete eighth symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished symphony' suggests Schubert's Eighth, but it is the Eroica minus its last letter A, after H from the end of 'eighth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic deeds or figures are on a grand scale, bigger and bolder than ordinary life.

clue.text: A collection of animals, millions, move quickly

parts.note: a zoo is a collection of animals
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Millions of zoo animals dash about.
explanation.definitionFit: To zoom is to travel very fast, which means to move quickly.

clue.text: He has depression, diamonds having been lost

indicators.note: having been lost means that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a downer is a depressing experience or a fit of low spirits
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A man is down in the dumps after losing his jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He has' is the definition: an owner is the one who has something.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who possesses something, the one who has it.

clue.text: Compound decrease —- lower most of aim

parts.note: to iron is to take creases out, so de-crease in the cryptic sense
to low is to moo, so a lower is a beast that lows, an ox

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an idea can be an aim or intention

explanation.surface: Instructions to reduce something and set the sights lower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decrease' is read as de-crease, to iron; 'lower' is the thing that lows, an OX. Rust is iron oxide.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron oxide, familiar as rust, is a chemical compound of iron and oxygen.

clue.text: It should improve the dial tone

definitions.text: It should improve the dial tone

parts.words: It should improve the dial tone
parts.note: seems to be about a telephone signal, but dial is slang for face and tone is skin tone

explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic cream rubbed into the skin is meant to improve the complexion of one's visage.

clue.text: Free pardon partly rejected, resulting in hanging

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A condemned prisoner's pardon is turned down, so he hangs.
explanation.walkthrough: The grim surface reads 'hanging' as execution; as a definition it means a hanging curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a curtain or cloth that hangs down, so it is a hanging.
